correctness.rationale: For all n>=2 and positive sitewise absorption rates, finite-dimensional dissipativity makes the bright Krylov span exactly the absorbed subspace. Independently reconstructing the Walsh eigenmode detector ranks gives 1 at k=0,n, n for interior k except n-1 at central k=n/2 when n is even. The invariant layer-affine space E has dimension n^2-n+2 and its even-dimensional missing normalized radial Krawtchouk vector q accounts for the parity term and both detector-addition consequences. Independent exact/numeric projector checks on n=2,3,4,5 reproduce dimensions 3,8,13,22 and sitewise formulas with errors below 1e-14. Finite tests corroborate, not prove, the all-n result.
